semantic_adjudication.reason: NL3 states both cruise and lane_change alternatives from enter_hwy share the identical guard conjunction dist_to_front<25 AND extra_lane=true. The exact closed-model triggers instead diverge: transition:line:27 (enter_hwy->cruise) fires on dist_to_front_25 (dist_to_front>=25), while transition:line:28 (enter_hwy->lane_change) fires on dist_to_front_25_extra_lane_true (dist_to_front<25 && extra_lane=true). This is a wrong-guard divergence from the NL-specified shared conjunction. The strongest alternative reading is that this is a beneficial, semantically mutually-exclusive resolution of the author-intended ambiguity: dist_to_front>=25 structurally complements the low-distance+lane condition, making the two alternatives disjoint by design rather than leaving them indistinguishable. This rebuttal is supported by the exact closed guard facts on both transitions but does not fully discharge the contract because the NL literal guard content for the cruise branch is changed rather than merely disambiguated, so the alternative reading survives as a competent rebuttal without defeating the underlying wrong-guard finding.

semantic_adjudication.reason: PlantUML line 21 first mentions FinishState inside the HighwayMode block ('cruise --> FinishState : dist_to_exit<2'), giving it an implicit parent of HighwayMode by first-mention semantics, yet lines 38 and 46 reference the same FinishState from lane_change_urban and UrbanMode, scopes outside HighwayMode. This establishes a wrong-scope containment defect: transitions from outside HighwayMode are routed into a state nested only inside HighwayMode. The strongest alternative reading is that the closed model is internally self-consistent (every reference resolves to the same single FinishState instance under HighwayMode), and the true divergence lies between the author's undeclared-state-first-mention convention and the requirement's intended flat/shared terminal state, rather than being an inconsistency introduced by the closed-model construction itself. This is a competent rebuttal regarding origin/attribution, supported by the exact source line facts, but it does not rebut the exact wrong-scope containment property under review, since the observed containment still fails to match the requirement's cross-scope structure.
semantic_adjudication.strongest_defeater: The closed model consistently routes every reference (lines 21, 38, 46) to one single FinishState nested under HighwayMode, so the model itself is internally coherent; the divergence originates from the author's own undeclared-state first-mention convention in the PlantUML source rather than from an error introduced during closed-model construction.

This exposes an unreachable composite scope needing a derived reachability contract, distinct from the satisfied owner-local initial-entry contract. (4) NL2 InitialState alternatives HighwayMode/UrbanMode use distinct guards (high_way_true vs urban_way_true) - not colliding. (5) enter_urban three-way alternatives use distinct triggers (dist_to_front_15_extra_lane_true, road_clear, intersection_true) - distinguishable, no candidate needed. (6) straight group (NL9) alternatives use intersection_true and dist_to_front_15_extra_lane_true - distinguishable, no candidate needed.

decisions.strongest_defeater: The two transitions may represent an intentional, semantically-equivalent disjoint resolution of the NL's shared-guard ambiguity (dist_to_front>=25 for cruise vs. dist_to_front<25 && extra_lane=true for lane_change), which achieves mutual exclusivity even though it alters the literal NL guard text for the cruise branch.
decisions.violated_obligation: The transition-group contract for enter_hwy requires both the cruise and lane_change alternatives to share the identical NL guard conjunction 'dist_to_front<25 AND extra_lane=true', with the model required to make them distinguishable despite the shared condition.

The exact closed-model triggers instead diverge: transition:line:27 (enter_hwy->cruise) fires on dist_to_front_25 (dist_to_front>=25), while transition:line:28 (enter_hwy->lane_change) fires on dist_to_front_25_extra_lane_true (dist_to_front<25 && extra_lane=true). issues.expected: Once HighwayMode transitions to FinishState via auto_finished=true, the system reaches a stable completion; FinishState should not itself continue into further active operating behavior.
issues.observed: FinishState is not a stable sink: the closed FCSTM gives FinishState outgoing edges 'FinishState -> [*] : /auto_finished_true effect { R45RouteToken = 20 }' (transition:line:36) and 'FinishState -> [*] : /urban_way_true effect { R45RouteToken = 22 }' (transition:line:40), both of which route back into the AutonomousMode-level HighwayMode<->UrbanMode dynamic-switch macro (transitions at lines 65 and 67, which are self-loop/HighwayMode->UrbanMode transitions), i.e., FinishState can re-enter continued mode-switching behavior rather than remaining a stable end state.
issues.reason: Per the termination frontier discipline, every termination contract requires auditing the exact target and active-ancestor continuations; a present edge into FinishState does not rebut the stronger property. Here FinishState itself carries outgoing transitions that route into continued HighwayMode/UrbanMode switching (guard R45RouteToken==20 self-loops HighwayMode, R45RouteToken==22 transitions to UrbanMode), so the designated ending target does not represent a stable completion but instead re-enters continued operating behavior.
issues.requirement_quote: The HighwayMode ends when the system transitions to FinishState, triggered by the `auto_finished=true` condition.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: These outgoing edges from FinishState are compiler-emitted macro segments realizing the same NL11 dynamic bidirectional HighwayMode<->UrbanMode transition group and the auto_finished self-loop declared at the AutonomousMode level (HighwayMode -> HighwayMode / HighwayMode -> UrbanMode), which are themselves independently required by NL11; one could argue FinishState's outgoing edges are simply inherited default hooks from the enclosing HighwayMode composite's boundary event handling (auto_finished_true, urban_way_true) rather than a bespoke re-entry authored specifically for FinishState, and do not represent an intentional cycle back into 'active driving' from a completed state.
